newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index strength continues.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index strength continues.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 0.8 percent to 311.51 at the start of play on Thursday.
The strength continued after the index broke through its 1996 high, recorded after the close of trade on Tuesday.
Day-on-day, Latin America climbed 1.0 percent to 585.87, Asia was up 0.8 percent at 260.18, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.6 percent at 142.72.

The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high last year of 308.77 on July 4, while its 275.79 low was recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was up 0.91 percent day-on-day at 169.99 at 0830 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high last year of 165.948 on July 3, and a 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was up 0.64 percent at 500.420, calculated after the close of trade on Tuesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. It touched a high last year of 505.452 on July 4, and recorded its 458.369 low on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.12 percent to 125.92 by the start of trade on Thursday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was flat at 103.95, Asia rose 0.09 to 132.61, and East Europe was up 0.20 at 162.69. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
